story.headline: EU proposes 22nd Russia sanctions package
story.summary: The European Commission proposed a 22nd sanctions package against Russia covering 60 banks, crypto, shadow-fleet tankers, ex-combatant visas and Russian athletes.
story.display_body: The European Commission proposed a 22nd package of sanctions against Russia on Monday 23 November, aimed at banks, crypto platforms, the "shadow fleet" of tankers, Russian ex-soldiers and Russian sport. Commission President Ursula von der Leyen said the package would extend the transaction ban to about 60 more Russian banks and remove all of them from SWIFT (the interbank messaging network), go after crypto and payment networks in Russia and in third countries that help it evade sanctions, and list more than 70 more shadow-fleet ships. It would also ban tankers insured in Russia, stop European firms from building, running or repairing Russian energy infrastructure (including electricity services for the first time), and bar Europeans from sitting on the boards of companies in Russia. It also proposes a visa ban on Russian ex-combatants, which she linked to "an escalation in non-conventional kinetic activities of Russian operatives in Europe". In sport, Russian teams and athletes competing under the Russian flag would be banned from events in the EU, and official Russian symbols could not be displayed. RFI notes that the sport and culture measures could be hard to agree because they can be seen as targeting Russian citizens directly. This is a proposal: it needs the unanimous approval of the 27 member states before it takes effect.
story.why: Switzerland usually adopts EU Russia packages a few weeks after Brussels (it took over the 21st on 4 November), so the bank, SWIFT and board-seat rules are likely to reach Swiss companies and banks next.

story.headline: Russia warns Estonia of 'open war'
story.summary: Russia's foreign ministry said Estonia's border closure and other actions are on the verge of triggering open war; Tallinn denies letting Ukraine use its airspace.
story.display_body: Russia's foreign ministry said on Monday 23 November that Estonia's actions are "on the verge of triggering open war", after summoning Estonia's chargé d'affaires in Moscow to protest Tallinn's plan to close its land border with Russia. Estonia says it will close all road crossings with Russia for at least six months from Tuesday 1 December, after it blamed Russian military intelligence for an attempted arson attack on a defence company near Tallinn; Russia denies involvement. Moscow also accused Estonia of "tacitly" letting Ukrainian drones use its airspace to strike north-western Russia, of obstructing Russian cargo ships in the Baltic, and of discriminating against ethnic Russians. Estonia's foreign ministry replied that it "has never allowed, and will never allow, its territory to be used for military operations by another country". NATO Secretary-General Mark Rutte said the alliance was monitoring the situation in Estonia and the recent Russian missile incursion into Poland.
story.why: Russia used claims that Russian speakers were being mistreated to justify moving into eastern Ukraine in 2014, and it is now saying the same about a NATO and EU member.

story.headline: Russian drone crosses into Poland
story.summary: A Russian drone briefly entered Polish airspace during an attack on western Ukraine, and a Russian strike on Zaporizhzhia killed two.
story.display_body: A Russian drone briefly entered Polish airspace late on Monday 23 November during an attack on western Ukraine, and a Russian strike on Zaporizhzhia early on Tuesday 24 November killed two people and wounded more than 40, including an infant. Poland's military said the drone was not shot down because of the risk to civilians, and Deputy Defence Minister Paweł Zalewski said he assumed the incursion was deliberate; it came three days after three Russian cruise missiles crashed in eastern Poland. Overnight, Russia's defence ministry said it intercepted 699 Ukrainian drones, and Moscow's mayor Sergei Sobyanin said 63 of them were shot down approaching the capital. Ukraine's air force said Russia launched 96 drones. On Monday, debris from Russian drones fell in central Kyiv near the presidential office and set a five-storey building on fire, injuring five people.

story.headline: EU caps hybrid car imports
story.summary: The European Commission imposed provisional safeguard import quotas on hybrid passenger vehicles from 1 December, implementing an understanding with China.
story.display_body: The European Commission imposed provisional import quotas on hybrid cars on Monday 23 November, to take effect on Tuesday 1 December. Each country that supplied more than 2% of the EU's hybrid imports in 2025 gets a quota of its 2025 volume plus a little over 15%, and all other countries share a single leftover quota; imports above the quotas are not allowed. The measure covers full hybrids, plug-in hybrids and mild hybrids, applies to imports from any country, and can last up to 200 days before final measures are decided. The Commission says it is putting into practice an understanding reached with China on 9 October to slow China's hybrid exports, and that EU carmakers are losing market share even though the market is growing. China asked the EU to stick to the "compliant and balanced" deal the two sides had reached.
story.why: a "safeguard" (an emergency trade tool against sudden import surges) sets a hard ceiling rather than a tariff, so it limits how many Chinese hybrids can reach European showrooms, whatever their price.

story.headline: UN: 47,000 women killed by relatives
story.summary: A UN Women/UNODC report says about 47,000 women and girls were killed by partners or family members in 2025.
story.display_body: About 47,000 women and girls were killed by partners or family members in 2025, or about five every hour, according to a report from UN Women and the UN Office on Drugs and Crime (UNODC) published on Tuesday 24 November. That is about 60% of the roughly 78,000 women and girls intentionally killed last year. The estimate draws on data from 122 countries and territories and is in line with the 45,000–51,000 range of recent years. Africa had the most such killings (22,100), followed by Asia (15,100), the Americas (7,400), Europe (2,100) and Oceania (300). The report says femicide (killing a woman or girl because she is female) is falling more slowly than homicide in general, especially in the Americas and Europe. It is published ahead of the International Day for the Elimination of Violence against Women on Wednesday 25 November.

story.headline: Russian jets trigger Ulleung shelter alert
story.summary: Russian military aircraft entered South Korea's air defence identification zone, prompting a brief shelter alert on Ulleung island.
story.display_body: Several Russian military aircraft entered South Korea's air defence identification zone over the East Sea (Sea of Japan) on Tuesday 24 November, and residents of Ulleung island were briefly told to take shelter. An ADIZ (air defence identification zone) is a buffer area beyond a country's own airspace where it identifies foreign aircraft. Yonhap first reported that a North Korean aircraft had violated South Korean airspace and then corrected this, and the military said the airspace was not violated. The interior ministry's alert to Ulleung residents was lifted after about five minutes. South Korea had scrambled fighter jets a week earlier when Russian aircraft entered the same zone.

story.headline: Pyongyang threatens to shut Swiss office
story.summary: Kim Yo Jong said North Korea will consider closing the Swiss diplomatic office over Swiss sanctions on a children's camp.
story.display_body: Kim Yo Jong, the influential sister of North Korean leader Kim Jong Un, said on Tuesday 24 November that Pyongyang will consider closing the Swiss diplomatic office that reopened there in October, because Switzerland has sanctioned a North Korean children's camp. In a statement carried by the state agency KCNA, she said that after the sanctions the Swiss office "has lost its raison d'être" and that it is "very doubtful" anything can be achieved with Bern while it follows "the line of London and Brussels". On 4 November Switzerland, like the EU and the UK, sanctioned the Songdowon international children's camp near Wonsan, which Bern says takes part in transferring Ukrainian children from occupied territories and in their "russification". The Swiss office has been working since Monday 19 October under the Swiss embassy in Beijing, after Foreign Minister Ignazio Cassis's visit to Pyongyang, the first by a Swiss foreign minister since 2003. The Federal Department of Foreign Affairs had not publicly responded by midday.
story.why: Switzerland is one of the few Western countries with a presence in Pyongyang and has long served as an informal channel to the West, and this shows how adopting EU sanctions can clash with that role.

story.headline: Greens challenge SVP Federal Council ticket
story.summary: The Greens nominated Geneva national councillor Delphine Klopfenstein Broggini to run against the SVP ticket in the 9 December Federal Council election.
story.display_body: The Greens nominated Geneva national councillor Delphine Klopfenstein Broggini on Monday 23 November to run against the SVP's two official candidates in the Federal Council election on Wednesday 9 December. Greens parliamentary group leader Greta Gysin called the SVP ticket "a provocation" and "an affront to Romandy and to women", because it leaves out Geneva national councillor Céline Amaudruz, the party's only female contender. Klopfenstein Broggini, 50, won the group's nomination over Vaud national councillors Léonore Porchet and Sophie Michaud Gigon after six rounds of voting. Political scientist Sarah Bütikofer told SRF that parliament is very likely to keep the seat with the SVP, and called the bid mainly a protest against the ticket, a year before the federal elections.

story.headline: Pension lump sums nearly double in a decade
story.summary: FSO: the median second-pillar lump sum rose to CHF 150,000 in 2025 from CHF 81,500 in 2015, as more retirees take capital.
story.display_body: The median lump sum taken from the second pillar (occupational pensions) rose to CHF 150,000 in 2025, from about CHF 81,500 in 2015, the Federal Statistical Office (FSO) said on Tuesday 24 November. About 73,700 people took a lump sum in 2025, 60% more than ten years earlier, while the number of new pension recipients, about 38,100, is back at its 2015 level after peaking at 45,300 in 2022. Of people receiving benefits from a pension fund, 48% took only capital, 33% only a pension and 18% both. The gender gap is large: the median new pension is about CHF 2,000 a month for men and CHF 1,300 for women, and the median lump sum is about CHF 216,800 for men and CHF 87,100 for women. The FSO notes that the figures are a snapshot of one year and do not show benefits drawn earlier or later.
story.why: more and more people are choosing a lump sum over a lifelong pension, which moves the risk of outliving their savings, and of investing them, from the pension fund to the retiree.

story.headline: FINMA finds 1,000 unlicensed insurance brokers
story.summary: FINMA found more than 1,000 insurance intermediaries working without authorisation and will raise the annual intermediary levy to CHF 1,575 from 2027.
story.display_body: The financial regulator FINMA said on Monday 23 November that it has found more than 1,000 insurance intermediaries working without authorisation since tougher supervision began in 2024, and that the yearly fee for registered intermediaries will rise from CHF 475 to CHF 1,575 from 2027. Since the revised Insurance Supervision Act took effect at the start of 2024, FINMA has removed about 3,200 entries from the register, some for violations and others because people stopped working or no longer met the requirements. FINMA says the problems were "considerably more serious than expected", ranging from missing qualifications and cold calling to wrong advice and fraud, and that in 2026 it ordered follow-up contacts with clients in several thousand cases. Part of the higher fee pays off a shortfall built up since 2024 and is expected to end after about ten years. Registration fees will also rise to CHF 675 for individuals and CHF 1,075 for companies. Anyone selling insurance in Switzerland must appear in FINMA's public register.
story.why: if someone who sold you an insurance policy is not in FINMA's register, they were not allowed to sell it, and FINMA's main concern is long-term or expensive products that buyers did not need.
